exams.title: Unit 1 Assessment: Vibe Coding Mindset and Environment Setup

questions.prompt: According to Andrej Karpathy's concept of 'Vibe Coding', what is the primary medium of creation for the developer?
options: Manual syntax and memory management
Natural language and strategic intent
Visual drag-and-drop block coding
Compiling binary code directly
questions.explanation: Vibe coding shifts the medium from rigid syntax (like semicolons) to natural language, where the creator acts as a director rather than a manual typewriter.
correctAnswers: Natural language and strategic intent

questions.prompt: Which of the following are components of the 'Vibe Coding' workflow as described in the course materials?
options: Strategic Intent
Manual Syntax Parsing
AI Generation
System Evaluation
Manual Memory Management
questions.explanation: The vibe coding workflow replaces manual syntax parsing and memory management with high-level intent, AI generation, and critical evaluation of the results.
correctAnswers: Strategic Intent
AI Generation
System Evaluation

questions.prompt: In the context of automation, ____ vibe coding occurs when an AI agent attempts to build an entire application without any human oversight, often leading to hallucination loops.
correctAnswers: Full
full

questions.prompt: What is the primary risk of adopting a 'Full Vibe Coding' approach without a human feedback loop?
options: The code will be too simple for professional use
The AI may enter recursive hallucination loops
The development process becomes too slow
The AI will refuse to generate multi-file structures
questions.explanation: Without human steering, AI agents often write overly complex code to patch minor bugs, leading to a loop of errors and hallucinations.
correctAnswers: The AI may enter recursive hallucination loops

questions.prompt: Which tasks are identified as 'AI Superpowers' because they rely on highly standardized patterns found in open-source data?
options: Generating UI boilerplates
Optimizing complex, custom database queries
Creating standard CSS styling
Writing basic database schemas
Implementing unique, high-security payment routing
questions.explanation: AI excels at standardized tasks like UI, CSS, and basic schemas because it has seen millions of these patterns; custom or complex logic is part of the 'Steering Zone'.
correctAnswers: Generating UI boilerplates
Creating standard CSS styling
Writing basic database schemas

questions.prompt: Modern AI models are optimized for ____ rather than truth, which can lead beginners into a false sense of security.
questions.placeholder: Enter the quality AI is optimized for
correctAnswers: plausibility

questions.prompt: What does the term 'context drift' refer to in AI-assisted development?
options: The AI forgetting the human's preferred coding language
The AI losing track of the overall application architecture
The shift from a local setup to a cloud setup
The time it takes for a prompt to be processed
questions.explanation: Context drift happens when an AI makes too many assumptions across a distributed project, leading to architectural inconsistencies.
correctAnswers: The AI losing track of the overall application architecture

questions.prompt: Identify the three critical checkpoints where a human must intervene in the vibe coding loop.
options: Intent Check
Syntax Compilation Check
Signature Check
Runtime Check
Hardware Compatibility Check
questions.explanation: The framework establishes Intent (goals), Signature (validity of tools), and Runtime (execution) as the three pillars of human oversight.
correctAnswers: Intent Check
Signature Check
Runtime Check

questions.prompt: The primary advantage of an AI-native IDE like Cursor over a cloud sandbox is its ability to ____ the entire local file system for better context.
questions.placeholder: Action the AI performs on files
correctAnswers: index

questions.prompt: In the human checkpoint framework, what is the purpose of the 'Signature Check'?
options: To verify the human's identity for security
To ensure the AI's generated plan matches the project goals
To confirm that suggested libraries and external tools actually exist
To check if the code runs without runtime errors
questions.explanation: The Signature Check is specifically used to spot hallucinations like non-existent API endpoints or libraries before attempting to run the code.
correctAnswers: To confirm that suggested libraries and external tools actually exist

questions.prompt: What are the primary disadvantages or 'trade-offs' of using a local environment like Cursor or VS Code?
options: Heavy cognitive load due to configuration errors
Inability to index the local file system
Potential 'installation paralysis' for beginners
Monthly subscription costs for the software itself
Responsibility for managing Node.js or terminal variables
questions.explanation: Local environments require the user to troubleshoot setup issues and manage software dependencies, which can be overwhelming for beginners.
correctAnswers: Heavy cognitive load due to configuration errors
Potential 'installation paralysis' for beginners
Responsibility for managing Node.js or terminal variables

questions.prompt: In the house-building metaphor, the traditional programmer is the bricklayer, while the vibe coder is the ____ directing an automated crew.
correctAnswers: architect

questions.prompt: An AI generates code using a method called 'Emailer.sendWithAutoRetry()'. If this method does not exist in any library, this is an example of:
options: Recursive logic
A syntax error
A confident hallucination
A runtime optimization
questions.explanation: AI models often generate plausible-sounding but non-existent functions based on statistical probability.
correctAnswers: A confident hallucination

questions.prompt: When acting as an 'Editor-in-Chief' of AI-generated code, what is the human responsible for?
options: Writing every semicolon by hand
Factual accuracy of the application
Overall quality of the output
Steering the AI with precise constraints
Compiling the AI's neural network
questions.explanation: The human 'owns' the result, ensuring it is accurate and high-quality, even if they didn't write the raw code.
correctAnswers: Factual accuracy of the application
Overall quality of the output
Steering the AI with precise constraints

questions.prompt: Which environment is described as a 'fully furnished apartment' because it requires zero setup for a developer?
options: A Local Engine Room
VS Code
A Cloud Sandbox (e.g., Replit)
A custom carpentry workshop
questions.explanation: Cloud sandboxes like Replit provide an integrated environment (editor, server, browser) immediately in the browser with no installation needed.
correctAnswers: A Cloud Sandbox (e.g., Replit)

questions.prompt: Which of the following are reasons why a developer might choose a Cloud Sandbox over a local IDE?
options: Eliminating installation paralysis
Speed-to-value for rapid prototyping
Lower cost for long-term production use
Ease of sharing a live preview link
Access to the user's full local file system
questions.explanation: Cloud sandboxes prioritize speed and accessibility, though they may have higher long-term costs and less local system access.
correctAnswers: Eliminating installation paralysis
Speed-to-value for rapid prototyping
Ease of sharing a live preview link

questions.prompt: Which project scenario is best suited for a local development environment?
options: A quick interactive calculator to show an investor
A personal website using a standard template
A highly secure application processing private local files
A simple landing page for a hobbyist project
questions.explanation: Local environments are preferred for security and privacy when handling local data, whereas cloud sandboxes are better for quick sharing and standard templates.
correctAnswers: A highly secure application processing private local files

questions.prompt: A developer needs to fix a 'hallucinated' function call in their project. Move the code block through the correct Human Checkpoint Framework sequence to validate the fix.
options: Intent Check -> Signature Check -> Runtime Check
Runtime Check -> Intent Check -> Signature Check
Signature Check -> Runtime Check -> Intent Check
Intent Check -> Runtime Check -> Signature Check
questions.explanation: The correct logical order is first ensuring the intent is right, then verifying the external signatures/APIs exist, and finally executing the code to check for runtime errors.
questions.animationHtml:
Interactive Checkpoint Sequencer

// Human Checkpoint Validation Pipeline
const validatedFix = processPipeline(codePatch);
Step 1
Step 2
Step 3
Intent Check
Signature Check
Runtime Check
Final Deployment
Drag labels into the steps to sequence the validation framework
correctAnswers: Intent Check -> Signature Check -> Runtime Check

exams.title: Unit 2 Assessment: Designing and Planning with AI

questions.prompt: According to the course materials, what is the 'absolute first superpower' a developer must develop in the world of vibe coding?
options: Mastering JavaScript syntax
Choosing the right battle (problem localization)
Integrating third-party APIs
Writing complex database schemas
questions.explanation: Session 2.1.1 emphasizes that success is decided before coding begins by choosing a clear, localized problem rather than trying to build 'The Everything App.'
correctAnswers: Choosing the right battle (problem localization)

questions.prompt: Which of the following are the three required components of a 'perfect single-sentence problem statement' as taught in Session 2.1.1?
options: The specific user
The technical database requirements
The exact moment of friction
The negative impact of that friction
The estimated development timeline
questions.explanation: A strong problem statement focuses on human friction (Who, When, and the resulting Pain) rather than technical implementation details like databases or timelines.
correctAnswers: The specific user
The exact moment of friction
The negative impact of that friction

questions.prompt: In the User Story framework, the '____' is considered the most critical element because it helps the AI understand underlying motivation for better UI suggestions.
questions.explanation: The 'Why' provides the emotional or practical payoff, allowing the AI to infer design needs that aren't explicitly stated in the technical requirements.
correctAnswers: Why

questions.prompt: Why does Session 2.1.3 advocate for 'aggressively pruning' features like user authentication and payment processing from a V1 MVP?
options: They are too expensive to implement
They lead to structural overload, AI hallucinations, and broken code
The AI does not know how to write security-related code
Most users do not want to create accounts for web apps
questions.explanation: Overloading the first prompt with complex features like security and payments increases the cognitive load and likely causes the AI to generate unreliable code.
correctAnswers: They lead to structural overload, AI hallucinations, and broken code

image.alt: The three pillars of a project description prompt.

questions.prompt: According to the 'Anatomy of a Project Description,' which of the following are the three core pillars of a clean prompt?
options: Core Purpose
User Experience (UX) Flow
Visual/Structural Layout
Monetization Strategy
Backend Infrastructure
questions.explanation: These three pillars act as a blueprint, ensuring the AI writes modular code without making incorrect assumptions about the application's intent or structure.
correctAnswers: Core Purpose
User Experience (UX) Flow
Visual/Structural Layout

questions.prompt: The 'V1 Definition Test' states that if a feature cannot be explained using 'If I click X, Y happens' without using technical words like ____, it does not belong in V1.
questions.explanation: V1 should focus on pure functional logic and interaction rather than infrastructure-heavy technical requirements.
questions.placeholder: Enter one of the forbidden technical words
correctAnswers: database
account
security

questions.prompt: What is the primary risk of using a vague prompt like 'Make a calculator'?
options: The AI will refuse to generate any code
The AI will charge more for the request
The AI falls back on statistical averages, producing generic or ugly output
The code will be written in a language your browser cannot read
questions.explanation: Without specific constraints, the AI uses its training data to provide a bare-bones solution that likely doesn't match your vision.
correctAnswers: The AI falls back on statistical averages, producing generic or ugly output

image.alt: Components of the Project Sandbox context.

questions.prompt: When establishing a 'Project Sandbox' (Context) for the AI, which elements should be included in the preamble?
options: The Tech Stack (tools)
The File Tree (existing assets)
Environment Limitations
The personal biography of the developer
Marketing slogans for the launch
questions.explanation: Providing context on tools, files, and limits prevents the AI from suggesting incompatible libraries or impossible architectures.
correctAnswers: The Tech Stack (tools)
The File Tree (existing assets)
Environment Limitations

questions.prompt: According to the unit material, the size of the problem you attempt to solve is ____ proportional to your likelihood of finishing it.
questions.explanation: The larger the problem (The Everything App), the more likely the project will fail due to complexity and scope creep.
correctAnswers: inversely

questions.prompt: How does providing a clear 'Why' in a user story affect the AI's code generation?
options: It increases the processing speed of the LLM
It allows the AI to suggest better UI layouts and workflows based on motivation
It forces the AI to use more complex Python libraries
It serves as a legal disclaimer for the generated code
questions.explanation: Understanding the 'Why' (the payoff) gives the AI a 'North Star' for making design decisions that benefit the end user.
correctAnswers: It allows the AI to suggest better UI layouts and workflows based on motivation

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of 'localized friction' suitable for a first AI project?
options: Tracking daily stretching intervals during meetings
Building a global social network for musicians
Logging plant watering dates to avoid overwatering
Designing a full-scale e-commerce platform with global shipping
A button that saves a water intake tally to local storage
questions.explanation: Localized friction involves small, manageable tasks that solve a specific problem without requiring massive infrastructure.
correctAnswers: Tracking daily stretching intervals during meetings
Logging plant watering dates to avoid overwatering
A button that saves a water intake tally to local storage

questions.prompt: The mindset shift for vibe coding requires the user to transition from a 'syntax writer' to an '____ of intent'.
questions.explanation: When using AI, the human role is to design the logical blueprint and intent, while the AI handles the specific syntax.
correctAnswers: architect

questions.prompt: What is the 'Memory Horizon' concept in Session 2.2.2 referring to?
options: The amount of RAM the user's computer has
The AI's tendency to forget project context without explicit prompts
The time it takes for a student to learn to code
The storage limit of a local database
questions.explanation: AI models behave like they have 'amnesia' regarding your specific setup unless you consistently provide context about your files and stack.
correctAnswers: The AI's tendency to forget project context without explicit prompts

questions.prompt: Why is using half-understood programming jargon or pseudo-code considered an anti-pattern for vibe coders?
options: It can confuse the AI's logical processing
It makes the prompt too short
It often leads to the AI misinterpreting the actual intent
It is illegal under most software licenses
Plain English is often more precise for communicating intent
questions.explanation: Vibe coding relies on clear natural language. Using jargon incorrectly creates a 'broken telephone' effect between the user and the AI.
correctAnswers: It can confuse the AI's logical processing
It often leads to the AI misinterpreting the actual intent
Plain English is often more precise for communicating intent

questions.prompt: In the comparison of the passenger and the driver, a driver told 'Take me somewhere cool' is confused. This illustrates that without ____, the AI will make assumptions to fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Explicit direction is required to prevent the AI from making guesses that lead to generic or buggy code.
correctAnswers: explicit direction

questions.prompt: In the 'Prompt Upgrade' workshop, what was the suggested way to specify buttons for a budgeting calculator?
options: Request the AI use 'Standard Input Elements'
Ask for 'Large, accessible buttons for arithmetic operations'
Provide a list of CSS hex codes for every button
Tell the AI to 'make it look like a real calculator'
questions.explanation: Specific descriptors for size and accessibility constrain the AI's creative choices to match the intended user experience.
correctAnswers: Ask for 'Large, accessible buttons for arithmetic operations'

questions.prompt: What are the characteristics of a successful 'V1 Win'?
options: It solves the core problem flawlessly
It is generated in a single or few predictable passes
It includes a fully functional SQL database
It builds momentum for the creator
It features professional-grade encryption
questions.explanation: A V1 win focuses on simplicity and functionality to ensure the project actually works and encourages further development.
correctAnswers: It solves the core problem flawlessly
It is generated in a single or few predictable passes
It builds momentum for the creator

questions.prompt: Which of these components should be avoided in a V1 MVP to keep the code footprint small?
options: Local browser storage
A single-tap action button
Image processing via external APIs
Real-time input history display
questions.explanation: External APIs and complex processing (like disease identification in the plant example) are too advanced for a V1 MVP.
correctAnswers: Image processing via external APIs

questions.prompt: You are building a 'Plant Care Tracker' V1. Use the 'MVP Prioritizer' to select the correct feature set for your initial AI prompt.
options: Watering Checklist
AI Disease Scanner
Community Chat Forum
Push Notification System
questions.explanation: A watering checklist represents the 'Core Value Proposition' without external API dependencies, making it a viable V1 target.
questions.animationHtml:
MVP Feature Prioritizer - Drag the single Core feature to the base of the pyramid

Drag your selected Core MVP feature to the base of the pyramid
Future
Nice-to-Have
Core (Base)
Watering Checklist
AI Disease Scanner
Community Chat Forum
Push Notification System
correctAnswers: Watering Checklist

exams.title: Unit 3 Assessment: Assembling and Understanding Code Foundations

questions.prompt: When generating a starter application with an AI, what is the main purpose of the 'Skeletal Prompt' technique?
options: To force the AI to use complex backend frameworks immediately
To establish a digital 'filing cabinet' with clear, lightweight structural boundaries
To generate a large amount of 'Lorem Ipsum' placeholder text
To automatically deploy the application to a cloud server
questions.explanation: A Skeletal Prompt ensures the AI creates a clean, minimal foundation (like a single index.html or a simple 3-file structure) without adding unnecessary bloat or complex external dependencies.
correctAnswers: To establish a digital 'filing cabinet' with clear, lightweight structural boundaries

questions.prompt: Which of the following are benefits of using 'Single-Page Application' (SPA) logic for a starter project as discussed in the unit?
options: It avoids the need for the user to walk through a 'new front door' (reload) for every interaction
It updates internal 'rooms' or views instantly
It requires a heavy Node.js server to function properly
It allows the app to feel like a single, cohesive house rather than separate, heavy pages
questions.explanation: SPAs are described as digital houses where views update instantly without full page reloads, providing a smoother experience. The material specifically warns against using heavy servers early on.
correctAnswers: It avoids the need for the user to walk through a 'new front door' (reload) for every interaction
It updates internal 'rooms' or views instantly
It allows the app to feel like a single, cohesive house rather than separate, heavy pages

questions.prompt: The process of defining spatial relationships and boxes in an interface before adding content is known as the ____ wire-up.
questions.explanation: The 'wireframe wire-up' is the conceptual metaphor used to help creators understand that code structure is simply a nested set of boxes and spatial relationships.
correctAnswers: wireframe

image.alt: Comparison of unstructured versus structured code layout.

questions.prompt: Why is it discouraged to ask an AI to 'build a dashboard' without first defining layout zones?
options: The AI will refuse to write any code at all
It prevents the AI from using any CSS styling
It forces the AI to make assumptions, often resulting in messy, unstructured code
Dashboards cannot be built using vanilla JavaScript
questions.explanation: Without specific layout zones (like header, sidebar, feed), the AI lacks a spatial roadmap and produces 'code spaghetti' based on its own guesses.
correctAnswers: It forces the AI to make assumptions, often resulting in messy, unstructured code

questions.prompt: What should a 'Directed Content Prompt' include to ensure high-quality output for page sections?
options: A request for 'Lorem Ipsum' to fill space
The specific tone and length of the text
The exact placement within the layout zones
Semantic headers like H1 or H2 to act as structural anchors
questions.explanation: Directed Content Prompts use semantic anchors and specific placement instructions to prevent the AI from generating unstructured 'div soup' or generic placeholder text.
correctAnswers: The specific tone and length of the text
The exact placement within the layout zones
Semantic headers like H1 or H2 to act as structural anchors

questions.prompt: When asking an AI for styling, the lesson recommends defining a ____ color for active elements like buttons or links.
questions.explanation: Defining a primary background and a specific accent color helps guide the AI toward a cohesive and intentional visual design system.
correctAnswers: accent

questions.prompt: According to the course, what is the danger of using 'Lorem Ipsum' during the initial build?
options: It makes the application run slower in the browser
It prevents the AI from being able to apply CSS styles
It makes it harder to evaluate if the application 'vibe' and purpose feel right
It is a deprecated web standard that modern browsers don't support
questions.explanation: Realistic, domain-specific text helps the creator and AI verify if the interface is actually meeting its functional goals, whereas generic text feels abstract.
correctAnswers: It makes it harder to evaluate if the application 'vibe' and purpose feel right

questions.prompt: To avoid 'vague styling prompts,' which constraints should you provide to the AI assistant?
options: The specific design system to use (e.g., Tailwind-style)
Maximum content widths (e.g., 1200px)
A request for the AI to 'surprise me' with the layout
Clear hover states and transition effects for buttons
questions.explanation: Vague prompts lead to unpredictable results; specific constraints like widths, design systems, and hover interactions produce stable, professional CSS.
correctAnswers: The specific design system to use (e.g., Tailwind-style)
Maximum content widths (e.g., 1200px)
Clear hover states and transition effects for buttons

questions.prompt: The 'dependency trap' occurs when the AI suggests importing complex third-party ____ too early in the project.
questions.explanation: Importing complex libraries or frameworks (like React) too early can introduce build-tool requirements that complicate the learning process and environment setup.
correctAnswers: libraries

image.alt: A layout diagram showing container relationships.

questions.prompt: In the context of 'Vibe Coding,' what does it mean to treat styling as a grid of containers?
options: Every element must be exactly the same size
Styling is about defining how boxes align, stack, and relate to each other spatially
You must draw a physical grid on your computer monitor
It refers to using a database to store CSS values
questions.explanation: Visual styling is built upon the structural layout; understanding how 'boxes' (containers) behave allows the creator to direct the AI more effectively.
correctAnswers: Styling is about defining how boxes align, stack, and relate to each other spatially

questions.prompt: Which of these are parts of the 'physical house' metaphor for software components?
options: Root folder as the foundation
index.html as the walls
Config file as the utility meters
JavaScript as the furniture
questions.explanation: The lesson specifically maps root folders to foundations, HTML to walls/structure, and config files to utility hookups to demystify technical files.
correctAnswers: Root folder as the foundation
index.html as the walls
Config file as the utility meters

questions.prompt: To prevent the AI from generating unnecessary build tools, you should specify the use of ____ CDN links for external libraries.
questions.explanation: CDN links allow you to include external styles or features without needing a complex local build environment or installation process.
correctAnswers: simple

questions.prompt: When the teacher asks students to identify 'instruction clutter,' what are they looking for?
options: Code that has too many comments
A prompt that mixes design, features, and structure in a chaotic way
A folder structure with too many files
An interface that uses more than three colors
questions.explanation: Cluttered instructions confuse the AI. Clean prompts separate structural needs from content and aesthetic styles for better results.
correctAnswers: A prompt that mixes design, features, and structure in a chaotic way

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of 'layout zones' mentioned in the unit material?
options: Global Header
Side-by-side dashboard
Bottom status bar
Background Database
questions.explanation: The unit focuses on visual zones (header, dashboard, status bar) that a user can see and define spatially in their layout instructions.
correctAnswers: Global Header
Side-by-side dashboard
Bottom status bar

questions.prompt: Adjust the application's layout to be responsive for a mobile device.
options: Horizontal Layout
Grid Layout
Stacked Layout
Hidden Sidebar
questions.explanation: Responsive design typically involves moving from a horizontal multi-column layout to a single vertical 'Stacked Layout' at the mobile breakpoint.
questions.animationHtml:
Interactive Responsive Layout Device Frame

Horizontal Grid Hidden Sidebar Stacked
Drag the slider to test layout reflows for different devices.
correctAnswers: Stacked Layout

exams.title: Unit 4 Assessment: Safe Vibe Coding and Rigorous Debugging

questions.prompt: You notice your app's UI looks beautiful and features an unrequested dark mode, but the core 'Delete Task' button you specified in your MVP goals is missing. This is an example of:
options: Feature Drift
Functional Parity
Requirement Validation
The Mirage of Completeness
questions.explanation: Feature Drift occurs when AI models add unrequested aesthetic features while neglecting the core structural requirements defined in the initial spec.
correctAnswers: Feature Drift

questions.prompt: Which of the following are columns in the 'MVP Alignment Matrix' used to audit an application's progress?
options: Target Requirement
Actual Behavior
Gap Status
AI Prompt History
Visual Vibe Score
questions.explanation: The MVP Alignment Matrix uses three specific columns to track what was requested versus what was delivered: Target Requirement, Actual Behavior, and Gap Status.
correctAnswers: Target Requirement
Actual Behavior
Gap Status

questions.prompt: In software testing, the standard, ideal path where a user completes a journey without any errors is known as the ____.
correctAnswers: Happy Path

image.alt: Example of a boundary value error in a shopping cart.

questions.prompt: If an online store allows a user to enter a quantity of '-5' and calculates a negative total, which category of disruptive input is being exploited?
options: Type Mismatch
Empty or Null Input
Boundary and Extreme Values
Logic Injection
questions.explanation: Entering negative numbers or zero where positive integers are expected is a test of boundary and extreme values.
correctAnswers: Boundary and Extreme Values

questions.prompt: When auditing an app for mobile responsiveness using browser developer tools, which specific visual bugs should you look for?
options: The Spillover (text clipping)
The Squish (unclickable buttons)
The Stack-Up (overlapping elements)
The Code Bloat (excessive CSS lines)
The Ghost Script (unused variables)
questions.explanation: These three represent the primary layout failures identifiable through visual inspection on different viewport sizes.
correctAnswers: The Spillover (text clipping)
The Squish (unclickable buttons)
The Stack-Up (overlapping elements)

questions.prompt: When a layout fails on mobile, the most common indicator visible to the user is a ____ scrollbar.
correctAnswers: horizontal

questions.prompt: Why is it important to document the 'Actual Result' even if it just feels 'vibe-y' or slightly laggy?
options: Minor lags can escalate into critical failures under high network loads
It helps the AI determine the color palette of the app
Subjective feelings are more important than console errors
It prevents the developer from having to write a prompt
questions.explanation: Small visual glitches or delays are often symptoms of underlying logic issues that break completely in different environments.
correctAnswers: Minor lags can escalate into critical failures under high network loads

questions.prompt: What are the primary goals of a 'Defensive Prompt' when fixing input vulnerabilities with an AI?
options: Validate the input to prevent processing of bad data
Display a helpful, friendly error message to the user
Ignore the error silently to keep the UI clean
Ask the AI to rewrite the entire application from scratch
Ensure the app doesn't crash or display 'NaN'
questions.explanation: Defensive prompts should focus on validation, user feedback, and stability rather than silent failures or total rewrites.
correctAnswers: Validate the input to prevent processing of bad data
Display a helpful, friendly error message to the user
Ensure the app doesn't crash or display 'NaN'

questions.prompt: To test your application on various screen sizes without owning multiple devices, you should use the ____ simulation mode in your browser.
correctAnswers: device

questions.prompt: In the 'Mirage of Completeness' analogy, what does the 'flashy mansion with a missing staircase' represent?
options: A highly secure application
An AI-delivered app that looks good but has broken core logic
A perfectly built MVP
A backend server without a frontend
questions.explanation: AI models often generate polished UIs (the mansion) while forgetting critical functional pathways (the staircase).
correctAnswers: An AI-delivered app that looks good but has broken core logic

questions.prompt: Which steps are involved in performing a 'Structured User Flow' audit?
options: Mapping out a user journey without looking at code
Recording 'Expected' vs 'Actual' results in a grid
Randomly clicking buttons to see what happens
Evaluating response times and visual transitions
Scanning the source code for syntax errors
questions.explanation: Structured auditing focuses on the user experience and documented outcomes rather than code inspection or random clicking.
correctAnswers: Mapping out a user journey without looking at code
Recording 'Expected' vs 'Actual' results in a grid
Evaluating response times and visual transitions

questions.prompt: The 'Input Filter' analogy describes ____ as a polite security guard checking credentials before data enters the logic engine.
correctAnswers: validation

questions.prompt: When you find a way to break your app using 'Wild Path' inputs, you should consider this a:
options: Failure of your coding skills
Sign that the AI model is useless
Major victory in the testing process
Reason to delete the project
questions.explanation: Finding bugs is the goal of testing; it allows you to identify and fix vulnerabilities before users encounter them.
correctAnswers: Major victory in the testing process

questions.prompt: When reproducing a problem, what information is essential to document?
options: The exact navigation pathway taken
The specific keys pressed or data entered
The developer's mood during the crash
The browser and environment details
The original prompt used to build the feature
questions.explanation: Reliable reproduction requires a scientific record of the environment and the sequence of actions that triggered the error.
correctAnswers: The exact navigation pathway taken
The specific keys pressed or data entered
The browser and environment details

questions.prompt: When a text element expands beyond its container and is cut off on a mobile screen, this is called the ____.
correctAnswers: Spillover

questions.prompt: What is the primary danger of 'Scope Creep by Proxy' in AI-assisted development?
options: The app becomes too cheap to host
The AI adds complex, unrequested features that introduce new bugs
The developer has to write too much manual code
The app's colors become inconsistent
questions.explanation: Scope Creep by Proxy happens when AI adds features you didn't ask for, which can complicate the codebase and hide flaws in core requirements.
correctAnswers: The AI adds complex, unrequested features that introduce new bugs

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid immediately prompting the AI with 'it's broken, fix it' when you find a bug?
options: It can lead to bloated or messy code workarounds
The AI might introduce 'fix' code that breaks other features
AI models are physically unable to understand that phrase
You haven't yet isolated the specific cause for the AI to target
It costs more tokens than a descriptive prompt
questions.explanation: Vague prompts lead to vague solutions. Isolating the problem first ensures the AI applies a 'surgical' and clean fix.
correctAnswers: It can lead to bloated or messy code workarounds
The AI might introduce 'fix' code that breaks other features
You haven't yet isolated the specific cause for the AI to target

questions.prompt: Investigate why the 'Submit' button on this mobile layout is unresponsive.
options: The button is overlapping a transparent div (The Stack-Up)
The button has shrunk too small to be clicked (The Squish)
The text has overflowed the button boundary (The Spillover)
The layout has a horizontal scrollbar preventing access
questions.explanation: In mobile viewports, elements often lose their 'tap target' size due to lack of space, making them physically impossible to interact with.

exams.title: Unit 5 Assessment: Deploying, Versioning, and Maintaining Applications

questions.prompt: You are building a complex new feature but aren't sure if the AI's code will break your existing project. What is the safest visual model to follow according to the course material?
options: Create a 'mega-commit' after the feature is finished and tested
Create an experimental branch to isolate the new code from the main timeline
Keep the project uninitialized to prevent tracking bad code
Undo changes manually using Ctrl+Z repeatedly until the app works again
questions.explanation: Branching creates a 'parallel universe' or sandbox where experimental leaps can be made without risking the stable 'main' branch.
correctAnswers: Create an experimental branch to isolate the new code from the main timeline

questions.prompt: Which of the following are true regarding the initialization of a repository (repo)?
options: It transforms a passive folder into an active environment with a 'flight recorder'.
It requires an active internet connection to GitHub to function.
It creates a hidden folder called .git to store the project history.
It automatically saves every change you make to the cloud.
It allows the system to identify 'untracked' files inside the folder.
questions.explanation: Initialization is a local process that sets up tracking via the .git folder; it does not require the internet or cloud syncing by default.
correctAnswers: It transforms a passive folder into an active environment with a 'flight recorder'.
It creates a hidden folder called .git to store the project history.
It allows the system to identify 'untracked' files inside the folder.

questions.prompt: To transform a standard folder into a Git repository locally, you would use the command 'git ____'.
correctAnswers: init

questions.prompt: What is the primary danger of the 'mega-commit' in vibe coding?
options: It makes the repository folder size too large for local storage.
It forces you to roll back multiple unrelated working features if only one part fails.
It prevents the AI from being able to read your code history.
It automatically publishes your experimental code to the live server.
questions.explanation: If unrelated changes (like styling and logic) are in one commit, you cannot revert a bug in the logic without also losing the styling work.
correctAnswers: It forces you to roll back multiple unrelated working features if only one part fails.

questions.prompt: When writing a semantic commit message, which prefixes are recommended for better organization?
options: feat: for new features
fix: for bug corrections
update: for any general change
save: for daily progress
style: for visual layout adjustments
questions.explanation: The material specifically highlights 'feat:' and 'fix:' as standard semantic prefixes to create a clear index for humans and AI.
correctAnswers: feat: for new features
fix: for bug corrections

questions.prompt: When a file is newly created in an initialized repository but not yet added to a commit, it is marked as ____.
correctAnswers: untracked

questions.prompt: Which zone acts as the 'packing box' where you prepare specific files before they are permanently saved to the repository?
options: Working Directory
Staging Area
Main Branch
Live Hosting Server
questions.explanation: The Staging Area is the middle ground where you choose which changes to include in your next commit 'parcel'.
correctAnswers: Staging Area

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of using a version control 'timeline' as discussed in the sessions?
options: It provides a guaranteed recovery point if AI-generated code crashes the app.
It automatically gathers user feedback from the internet.
It allows learners to experiment with 'creative leaps' safely.
It removes the need for human developers to write any code.
It acts as a 'time machine' to warp back to previous save states.
questions.explanation: The timeline visualization emphasizes safety, recovery, and the freedom to experiment without permanent consequences.
correctAnswers: It provides a guaranteed recovery point if AI-generated code crashes the app.
It allows learners to experiment with 'creative leaps' safely.
It acts as a 'time machine' to warp back to previous save states.

questions.prompt: The strategy of using Git to feel safe while letting an AI generate experimental code is referred to in the course as ____ coding.
correctAnswers: vibe

questions.prompt: Why should a 'vibe coder' check their active branch status before prompting an AI assistant?
options: To ensure the AI is using the latest version of the cloud repository
To avoid making accidental experimental changes on the stable main branch
To verify that the local repository has an active internet connection
To trigger an automatic commit before the AI generates new code
questions.explanation: If you are not on your experimental branch, the AI's generated code will overwrite your stable production code on the main branch.
correctAnswers: To avoid making accidental experimental changes on the stable main branch

questions.prompt: Which actions are part of the 'two-step dance' of saving a commit?
options: Initializing the repository
Staging the precise files that belong to the change
Committing the staged files with a clear message
Publishing the code to a live hosting platform
Creating a new branch for every single line of code
questions.explanation: Committing is described as a two-step process: moving changes to the Staging Area (packing) and then to the Repository (shipping).
correctAnswers: Staging the precise files that belong to the change
Committing the staged files with a clear message

questions.prompt: In the analogy of the 'messy desk,' which Git component represents the 'shipped parcel'?
options: The Working Directory
The Staging Area
The Repository
The Experimental Branch
questions.explanation: The Repository is the final destination for staged changes, representing the completed and logged history of the project.
correctAnswers: The Repository

questions.prompt: According to the course, what should a high-quality commit message include?
options: A short, active-verb summary of the change.
A complete list of every character modified.
A brief explanation of *why* the change was made.
A semantic prefix like 'feat:' or 'fix:'.
The name of the AI assistant that generated the code.
questions.explanation: Good commits are semantic and document intent ('why') rather than just the 'what'.
correctAnswers: A short, active-verb summary of the change.
A brief explanation of *why* the change was made.
A semantic prefix like 'feat:' or 'fix:'.

questions.prompt: What happens visually in your workspace when you switch from an experimental branch back to the main branch?
options: The experimental code is automatically merged into the main branch.
The experimental changes disappear, and the app restores to its stable state.
The project folder is deleted to make room for the main branch.
A notification is sent to the AI to stop generating code.
questions.explanation: Switching branches acts like a portal, swapping the files in your folder to match the selected point in history.
correctAnswers: The experimental changes disappear, and the app restores to its stable state.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to learn the 'Why' of version control before learning specific commands?
options: To build a strong visual intuition of history as a timeline.
To reduce the paralyzing fear of breaking working code.
Because terminal commands are no longer used in modern development.
To understand that version control is a safety net for experimentation.
To ensure the student knows how to fix hardware issues.
questions.explanation: The course focuses on conceptual whiteboard sessions to build confidence before introducing technical syntax.
correctAnswers: To build a strong visual intuition of history as a timeline.
To reduce the paralyzing fear of breaking working code.
To understand that version control is a safety net for experimentation.

questions.prompt: How does a 'micro-commit' strategy help when building a multi-part feature?
options: It allows you to save your work every 30 seconds automatically.
It ensures that you only commit when a specific task works and the app doesn't crash.
It prevents the .git folder from becoming too complex.
It makes the deployment to the live server much faster.
questions.explanation: Micro-commits focus on discrete, functional states, making it easier to identify exactly where a problem might have been introduced.
correctAnswers: It ensures that you only commit when a specific task works and the app doesn't crash.

questions.prompt: Once an experiment on a branch is successful, what are the possible next steps?
options: The branch can be merged back into the main timeline.
The branch must be deleted immediately to save space.
The code can be deployed to a live hosting platform.
The branch can be discarded if the experiment was actually a failure.
The main branch should be deleted to favor the experimental one.
questions.explanation: Branches are flexible; they can be integrated into the main project if successful or thrown away if the experiment fails.
correctAnswers: The branch can be merged back into the main timeline.
The branch can be discarded if the experiment was actually a failure.

questions.prompt: The project is currently at Commit C (Broken). You need to restore the project to the last stable state, Commit B.
options: Delete the .git folder and restart
Merge the broken code into the Main branch
Move the HEAD pointer back to Commit B
Create a new branch from Commit C
questions.explanation: Returning to an earlier version is like moving a record player needle (the HEAD pointer) back to a previous track (Commit B) where the app was stable.
